# Writing Plan — symb_invariant_consensus
# Updated: 2026-05-20T20:00:00Z
# V3 FRAMING: G+R Dual Method Paper (Director D091 V3)
# Target: EMNLP 2026 ARR May cycle

meta:
  venue: EMNLP 2026
  track: main (ARR May cycle)
  template: docs/paper/acl.sty
  page_limit: 8
  deadline: 2026-05-25
  title: >
    Breaking Symbolic Confirmation Bias: Constraint-Answer Decoupling
    and Cross-Architecture Verification for LLM Logical Reasoning
  core_claim: >
    Symbolic confirmation bias (4.97× bias ratio) causes self-extracted
    FOL constraints to confirm LLM trace answers regardless of correctness.
    Two independent cures with different mechanisms: (1) Constraint-Answer
    Decoupling (G) truncates trace conclusions (4.1% text), cutting the
    conclusion→FOL causal path (+11.3pp vs SC, +6.4pp vs SICA on 70/204
    intermediate); (2) Cross-Architecture NLI Verification (R) uses
    encoder-only DeBERTa-large as architecturally independent verifier
    (+4.41pp, p=0.039). G=information-flow intervention, R=architectural
    diversity. Both independently validate the causal model.
  paper_type: >
    Dual positive method paper: diagnosis (confirmation bias) + two
    independent solutions with different mechanisms (G=info-flow, R=arch-diversity)
  framing: >
    D091 V3: G is PRIMARY method (causal intervention), R is SUPPLEMENTARY
    (architectural diversity verification). Both together demonstrate
    confirmation bias is solvable through orthogonal paths.
  created_at: 2026-05-19T20:30:00Z
  updated_at: 2026-05-20T20:00:00Z
  previous_version: "v2.1 (2026-05-20T18:00): D091 V2 R-only reframe"

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contributions (5)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
contributions:
  - id: C1
    label: "Symbolic Confirmation Bias Quantification + Causal Model"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      First quantification of Symbolic Confirmation Bias: 4.97× bias ratio,
      83.3% wrong-answer constraint support, 94% error overlap with SC.
      Causal chain: model→answer→FOL→aggregation≈SC. Oracle gold-FOL
      proves mechanism sound (+14.22pp FOLIO, +11.50pp PW, p<0.001).
    registry_refs: [exp-confirmation-bias, exp-031, exp-022]

  - id: C2
    label: "Constraint-Answer Decoupling (G) — PRIMARY METHOD"
    status: PENDING_REGISTRY
    claim: >
      Truncating trace conclusions (4.1% text) before FOL extraction
      cuts the conclusion→FOL causal path. +11.3pp vs SC, +6.4pp vs SICA
      (70/204 intermediate). Causal proof: minimal text removal (4.1%)
      yields maximal effect, confirming bias concentrates in conclusion
      sentences. Zero-cost intervention requiring no additional model.
    registry_refs: [exp-wave3-dir-g-decoupling]
    data_note: >
      Director-provided numbers from 70/204 intermediate subset.
      Registry status=RUNNING. Full 204/204 results pending.
      Numbers MUST be verified against registry when DONE.
    intermediate_data:
      n_evaluated: 70
      n_total: 204
      conservative_accuracy: 0.657
      sc_baseline: 0.5441
      sica_baseline: 0.5931
      delta_vs_sc_pp: 11.3
      delta_vs_sica_pp: 6.4
      avg_truncation_ratio: 0.041

  - id: C3
    label: "Cross-Architecture NLI Verification (R) — SUPPLEMENTARY"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      DeBERTa-large NLI (encoder-only, 350M) as architecturally independent
      verifier. Combo w=3: 58.82% (+4.41pp, p=0.039). NLI∩SC: 68.48%@45%.
      Per-label: NLI False 71.43% vs SC 38.10% (+33pp).
      Mechanism: architectural diversity (encoder vs decoder).
    registry_refs: [exp-wave3-dir-r-nli-verifier, exp-wave3-dir-r-combo-extended]

  - id: C4
    label: "25+ Intervention Failure Taxonomy + Independence-Accuracy Frontier"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      25+ same-model remediation strategies all fail. Independence-accuracy
      Pareto frontier: Debate κ=0.15 but -18.6pp; SC/DP/ICG cluster at
      κ≈0.40-0.47. Three model families all κ≥0.41.
    registry_refs: [exp-077, exp-076, exp-074, exp-075b, exp-cross-model-phase1]

  - id: C5
    label: "Process-κ: Reasoning Homogeneity Deeper Than Answer Agreement"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      CoT cosine similarity (0.69) far exceeds answer-κ (0.41),
      r=-0.06 (p=0.36). 9.3% trace pairs show convergent reasoning.
    registry_refs: [exp-wild4-process-kappa]

Now I have a thorough understanding of the paper. Let me also read the paper-writing-norms skill and the paper-quality-lessons skill as required before planning.

Actually, let me first analyze the current state and design the restructuring plan. Let me think about the key issues:

1. **Current structure** (8 sections in main text + appendix):
   - §1 Introduction (~1.3 pages)
   - §2 Related Work (~1 page)
   - §3 Background & Setup (~1.5 pages with Figure 1, equations, Mirage hypothesis)
   - §4 Experiments (~0.7 pages - just setup paragraph and Table 1)
   - §5 Analysis (~1.5 pages with Figure 2, Table 5 border)
   - §6 Cross-Architecture Proof-of-Concept (~0.5 pages)
   - §7 Discussion and Conclusion (~0.3 pages)
   - Limitations (~0.3 pages)

Looking at the actual structure in main.tex, I see the sections are: abstract, introduction, related work, method, and experiments, though the experiments section appears to be incomplete or cut off in what I'm seeing.

Let me trace through the file structure more carefully. The main.tex loads abstract, introduction, related_work, method, experiments, analysis, solutions, discussion, and a limitations section. So there are 7 numbered sections total. The experiments file contains §4 with subsections for Setup and Main Results including Table 1, but I need to verify what comes after that in the full document structure. .tex is actually the file being used, not diagnosis.tex. Let me verify the structure by checking what main.tex actually includes — it looks like experiments.tex is the active file at line 66, which means diagnosis.tex is probably an older version that's no longer part of the document. Looking at the analysis.tex file, it contains a full Analysis section with subsections covering Condorcet Effective-K, Symbolic Confirmation Bias, Process-Level Independence, and Remediation Analysis, along with several tables and figures including the frontier, independence, and generalization results. So diagnosis.tex appears to be a duplicate or abandoned version that's not actually included in the compiled paper. So diagnosis.tex is likely an earlier draft that didn't make it into the final document. Now looking at what the Director wants me to address: there are too many technical abbreviations cluttering the paper. I need to identify which ones are truly essential—SC and SICA are the core comparison, BR is the central metric, and $K_\text{eff}$ and $C_0$ are key diagnostics. The rest like CJT, CCR, DRC, ICG, and ProcessSim can either be spelled out inline or moved to the appendix to reduce cognitive load.

There's also a serious imbalance in how space is allocated. The Condorcet Jury Theorem derivation takes up half a page when it's well-established and could be condensed to just the key equation in a couple lines. Meanwhile, the remediation section with 27 strategies that all fail is only getting about 15 lines—that's the most surprising finding and deserves much more attention. The discussion section is also underdeveloped at just a third of a page, especially given how strong the result is with three diagnostics perfectly classifying 60 conditions.

Pages 3-5 are also a dense text wall with no visual breaks. Figure 1 is stuck on page 2 in the introduction and Table 1 doesn't appear until page 6 in the experiments section, leaving the middle section feeling heavy and hard to parse.

I'm also noticing the framing of the Symbolic Mirage Hypothesis needs work. Right now it's presented as O1, O2, P1, but O1 and O2 are actually observations discovered during the experiments, not predictions. Looking back at the method file, it does frame them as "two observations motivate the hypothesis" followed by a testable prediction, which is clearer. I should make sure that distinction is sharp throughout.

On the cross-architecture escape claim, I need to be more careful with the significance statement. The +6.67pp result only holds for Mistral-7B, so calling it significant across the board overstates the finding. I should present this as preliminary evidence rather than a strong claim. — but the summary claims 39.17/+15.83/+7.00. There's a clear mismatch between what the summary says was updated and what's actually in the files right now. The introduction.tex also shows the older +6.67 values, which suggests either the changes weren't saved properly or the file got reverted somehow. I need to figure out which version is correct and whether these edits actually persisted.

But I'm getting sidetracked on data consistency when the Director is really asking for a strategic restructuring plan. Let me step back and think about how to reorganize the paper holistically.

Looking at the current layout, I've got seven sections spread across eight pages. The introduction is dense but solid at about 1.3 pages, though the contribution list runs long. Related work covers four paragraphs in roughly a page. Background takes up 1.5 pages with the CJT derivation, SICA pipeline, and the Mirage Hypothesis boxes. Experiments is quite compressed at 0.7 pages with just setup and main results.

The real bulk is in Analysis—1.5 pages with four subsections, three tables, and two figures. Cross-Architecture is squeezed into half a page with one table and dense text. Discussion is painfully short at 0.3 pages.

The fundamental problem is that the paper reads like a diagnostic investigation rather than a discovery narrative. It sets up in section 3, shows a null result in section 4, then spends section 5 diagnosing what went wrong, section 6 offering an escape hatch, and section 7 wrapping up in barely two paragraphs. There are thirteen abbreviations scattered throughout, and no figures appear until page six.

The strongest contributions are actually the Symbolic Mirage finding and the diagnostic insights, but they're buried in a structure that makes the paper feel like a postmortem rather than a forward-looking contribution.

The core issue is ambition—the paper tries to cover 27 remediation strategies, 9 models, 60 conditions, 3 diagnostics, 2 positive results, and 4 analysis subsections in just 8 pages. Everything gets shortchanged.

I think the solution is to reorganize the narrative flow entirely. Instead of the current diagnostic-heavy structure, I'd merge and redistribute sections to highlight what actually matters. The Introduction should be sharper and cut the contribution list down. Related Work can be compressed. Then I'd restructure the middle sections to give proper breathing room to the Symbolic Mirage finding and the three diagnostics that classify the 60 conditions—that's where the real value is.

But I'm running into a page budget problem. Eight pages is really tight, and I need to count more carefully what actually fits.

The key moves are: push the CJT math into the intro as just an equation to save space, then present the Mirage Hypothesis after the data shows it rather than stating it upfront. Merging the experiments and analysis sections eliminates that awkward gap where results sit separate from explanation. I should also tighten those contribution bullets—they're taking up too much real estate right now—and find room for a figure around page 3 or 4, probably the regime scatter plot. The discussion needs actual breathing room to handle the diagnostics properly.

For the narrative arc, the story is cleaner if I lead with the natural progression: saturation in standard solvers suggests extracting formal constraints, we built SICA with Z3, but it fails—and that failure reveals Symbolic Confirmation Bias where the constraints just echo what the model already believed. Then I show how deep this goes with process-level correlation and why 27 remediation attempts all flopped. The payoff is that cross-architecture verification actually works, and the three diagnostics give practitioners a real tool to predict which of the 60 conditions will break.

For the 8-page structure, the introduction hooks on the paradox—formal verification should help LLMs but doesn't—and previews the diagnosis and solution in one tight narrative. Background and method compress into a single page with the SICA pipeline, the key definitions, and experimental setup all together; I'm dropping the Condorcet subsection since the core idea gets mentioned upfront. Results expand to 1.5 pages to show Table 1 in full, the three regime types, and the scatter plot moved up from the appendix so readers see the pattern immediately.

The diagnosis section becomes the centerpiece at 2 pages, where I present the Mirage Hypothesis as something that emerged from the data rather than assumed beforehand, backed by the SCB quantification, process-level independence evidence, and an expanded explanation of why remediation fails. Then the escape section wraps up with cross-architecture NLI as the main result, the capability gap, domain adaptation, and the three diagnostics framed as a practical toolkit for practitioners.

For Related Work, I'm reconsidering the placement — moving it after results would be unconventional for ACL/EMNLP venues, so I'll keep it at section 2 but trim it down. The real issue is that pages 3-5 form a text wall because they contain the tail end of the introduction, all of Related Work, and the start of Method with equations and hypothesis boxes. The bottleneck is Related Work itself, so compressing that section should help break up the density.

To address this, I could either add a figure to the Method section, move Table 1 earlier by integrating experimental setup into Method, or insert a conceptual diagram showing the bias ratio illustration. Option B feels strongest — merging the experimental setup into Method and presenting results right after means Table 1 appears around pages 4-5 instead of page 6, which naturally breaks up the text wall.

But stepping back, the Director's feedback about selecting 3-4 strongest contributions and deepening those while condensing the rest suggests I should identify what truly matters: the SCB quantification and shuffle control mechanism form the core contribution.

The independence-accuracy trade-off showing 27 failed strategies against three model families hitting the same ceiling is compelling. The three diagnostics that classify all 60 cases have strong practical appeal for reviewers. And the cross-architecture escape result points toward solutions.

What needs to shrink or move to appendix: the CJT derivation, process-level independence details, multi-seed replication specifics, TOST equivalence testing, and CCR analysis. This frees up space to develop the four strongest findings.

For the revised structure, I'm tightening the Introduction to 1 page with a sharper hook around the Z3 formal verification paradox and condensing the contribution list to three concise items.

Related Work compresses to 0.7 pages by merging the CJT paragraph into the SC discussion and cutting the repetitive positioning section down to three paragraphs total.

The SICA section stays at 0.8 pages but reorganizes: pipeline description with equations, experimental setup (models, datasets, parameters) moved up from §4.1, and I'm holding the Mirage Hypothesis and the two Empirical Finding boxes until §5 where they'll land as observations after the data appears.

Main Results expands slightly to 1.3 pages, with Table 1 now appearing around page 4-5 instead of page 6.

Now I'm structuring the regime analysis with Figure 2 to break up the text, adding a brief null-result summary and a one-to-two sentence mention of the oracle.

§5 gets a major overhaul—renaming it "The Symbolic Mirage" and opening with "Why does formal verification fail?" Then I'm layering in the SCB quantification with bias ratios and shuffle control, moving the interventions figure here for visual relief, keeping the cross-model bias table, condensing process-level independence to one paragraph, and expanding the independence-accuracy trade-off section which is currently too thin. The kappa generalization table stays, and I'm ending with the Mirage Hypothesis statement emerging from the data rather than presented upfront.

§6 softens the cross-architecture NLI findings to preliminary evidence and includes Table 3 on the capability gap, all within 1.0 page.

For §7, I'm covering implications for test-time scaling, framing when symbolic aggregation actually helps as a diagnostic framework, and touching on broader implications for self-correction and self-verification—keeping it to 0.6 pages.

The full draft lands around 7.4 pages, which feels right. I'm also trimming abbreviations: keeping SC, SICA, BR, and the effective kappa notation, but spelling out "symbolic confirmation bias" most of the time instead of SCB, writing out "Condorcet Jury Theorem" since it appears only a few times, and removing CCR from the main text entirely.

I'm pushing several other abbreviations to the appendix—DRC, TOST—and replacing things like ICG with "iterative constraint generation," ProcessSim with just "process similarity," and FOL with "first-order logic" or "logical constraints" spelled out. That cuts my abbreviation list from 13 down to about 6 core ones, which should make the paper much more readable.

For the Mirage Hypothesis, I'm restructuring §3 to introduce SICA as a neutral method without framing it as a hypothesis first, then letting §4 present the null results—this feels cleaner than the current hypothesis-driven setup.

The real narrative shift happens in §5, where I observe the pattern and formulate the hypothesis there, then test it with the shuffle control, cross-model, and cross-architecture experiments. That's a more natural scientific flow.

I'm also expanding the discussion from 2 short paragraphs to 3-4 fuller ones—first showing how the three diagnostics classify all 60 conditions as a practitioner tool, then discussing what this means for test-time scaling and self-verification, and finally adding a concrete decision tree for when symbolic aggregation actually helps.

I'm considering a new diagnostic decision tree figure for pages 3-5 that visualizes the thresholds for $C_0$, $K_\text{eff}$, and BR to guide practitioners.

Now I need to map out where each figure actually lands in the restructured layout—intro and pipeline on pages 1-2, related work and methods starting on 2-3, then Table 1 breaking up the text around pages 3-4, the regime scatter plot on 4-5, the symbolic mirage section with intervention tables on 5-6, and the kappa analysis with escaping results on 6-7.

Looking at what's truly essential versus what can move to the appendix, I should keep the pipeline figure, main results table, cross-model bias table, intervention strategies figure, escape results table, and capability gap scatter plot in the main text. The independence metrics table, process-kappa scatter, and kappa generalization table can shift to supplementary material since they overlap with or support the core claims without being critical to understanding them.

The real issue is the uneven distribution across pages—I have nothing on pages 3-5 but then everything clusters on pages 6-8. I need to spread these displays more evenly and cut the density down to around 3-4 figures and 3-4 tables total in the main text.

My plan is to move the regime scatter figure to page 4, consolidate the frontier bias and kappa generalization tables on page 5, put the interventions figure on page 6, then pair the NLI table with the capability gap figure on page 7. The independence table and process-kappa figure can go to the appendix since they overlap with other results. This leaves room for discussion and limitations on page 8.

I'm also thinking about whether I need a new diagnostic decision tree figure to show how the model classification works—something that walks through the logic of identifying degenerate cases based on the C₀ threshold and SICA values. The real insight here is that formal verification itself becomes meaningless when the extraction layer inherits the model's biases—Z3 is provably correct, the constraints pass validation, but the final answers still collapse to majority voting on most problems. This reframes the paper from "self-correction fails again" to "even sound formal methods can't escape the underlying model's limitations." The formal apparatus is a "mirage" — looks rigorous, does nothing. This framing should be front and center, though I won't push for a title change unless the Director asks. I could suggest something punchier like "The Symbolic Mirage: Why Provably Sound Verification Fails Under Self-Extraction" to highlight the paradox, but the current title works too. The Director mentioned high information density and needing to trim terminology, so simplification might help across the board.

Now I'm mapping out the full writing plan with word budgets. For an ACL 2-column format paper around 8 pages, I'm allocating roughly 4800 words for main text after accounting for figures and tables. Introduction gets about 800 words with Figure 1, Related Work around 560, Method & Setup about 720 with equations, and Results taking up the most space with Table 1 and scatter plots. I need to finish sketching out the remaining sections and their allocations. I'm mapping out the page budget more carefully now. The introduction needs to be tighter — I'll lead with a sharper hook about formal solvers failing to improve reasoning, then condense the contributions to three focused bullets and soften the cross-architecture claims while adding the power caveat about underpowered conditions. Related work gets compressed by merging the CJT discussion into the symbolic computation section and cutting redundant positioning material. Now I need to figure out how to structure the method section itself. & Setup (0.9 page)**  
Key changes:
- Keep SICA pipeline equations (essential)
- Move Mirage Hypothesis to §5 (presented as emerging from data)
- Remove the two Empirical Finding boxes from here
- Add experimental setup (models, datasets, parameters) — merge from current §4.1
- Keep $K_\text{eff}$ and $C_0$ definitions but make them inline

**§4 Results (1.3 pages)**
Key changes:
- Table 1 appears here (now on page ~4 instead of 6)
- Figure 2 (regime scatter) also here — breaks the text wall
- Condense regime analysis to essential points
- Move TOST/multi-seed details to appendix
- Brief oracle mention (1-2 sentences, details in appendix)

**§5 The Symbolic Mirage (1.8 pages)**
This section needs to be the analytical heart of the paper. I'll start by asking why sound verification breaks down, then dive into the SCB quantification with bias ratios and shuffle controls as the key finding. I'm including a cross-model bias table and a compact figure showing how 27 intervention strategies fail. The independence-accuracy trade-off deserves real expansion here—I'll develop it from 15 to 30 lines. Then I'll present the three diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) with clear decision boundaries, add a TikZ decision tree figure that shows the 60/60 classification, and wrap up by formulating the Mirage Hypothesis as something that emerges naturally from the data.

**§6 Cross-Architecture Escape (0.9 pages)**
Softening the language to "preliminary evidence" and including Table 3 on cross-

generator NLI. I'm adding a capability gap scatter figure and a brief paragraph on domain adaptation, then framing the whole section as testing whether our diagnostic predictions actually work in practice.

**§7 Discussion (0.6 page)**
Expanding this significantly to cover implications for test-time scaling, positioning the diagnostic tool for practitioners, discussing broader implications for self-verification methods, and outlining future directions like trained extractors and multi-modal approaches.

Now I'm reconsidering the framing of the core surprise. The current angle—self-consistency saturates, we tried symbolic constraints, they don't work—is fine, but there's a sharper way to tell it. Formal verification is the gold standard for correctness, Z3 is provably sound, and when we extract formally specified constraints from LLM reasoning traces, it should catch errors that majority voting misses. But it doesn't. That's the real tension.

The constraints pass syntactic validation at 99%, the solver itself is correct (oracle experiments show +30 percentage points of improvement is possible), yet the self-extracted constraints render the entire formal apparatus informationally equivalent to just counting votes. I'm calling this the Symbolic Mirage—it looks valid, the mechanism works in principle, but extraction introduces a systematic bias that defeats the purpose.

This framing lands harder because Z3 isn't just another LLM trick, it's a formal solver used in program verification; the constraints appear valid; the oracle proves the mechanism could work; and the failure is specifically in extraction, a new kind of bias distinct from "LLMs are bad at logic." That's different from Huang et al.'s finding that natural language self-correction fails—we're showing that formal self-verification fails even with a correct solver, because extraction inherits the same biases.

For the abstract, I should lead with the paradox: formal verification should improve reasoning, but we're showing that provably sound Z3 verification becomes informationally vacuous under self-extraction. Now I need to finalize the writing plan and figure out what additional analyses the Agent should generate—a decision tree flowchart showing the classification boundaries, verification of the solution values since there's a discrepancy between what's in the tex file and what I expect, and I should check if there's anything else critical missing.

Actually, looking back at the current writing_plan.yaml, it's built around a "G+R Dual Method" framing that doesn't match the actual paper anymore. The paper has evolved into a diagnostic study with a null result, analysis, and cross-architecture findings—there's no mention of constraint-answer decoupling anywhere. The plan is outdated and needs a complete rewrite to reflect what the paper actually is now.

The three real contributions are quantifying self-verification bias across models and strategies, establishing a diagnostic framework with effective constraint strength and baseline robustness, and analyzing process-level independence. My restructuring would elevate the diagnostic framework to equal prominence with the bias quantification, condense the process analysis as supporting evidence, and position the cross-architecture escape as validation rather than a formal contribution.

Let me draft a new writing plan that actually maps to this structure.

But first I need to address what the Director flagged about the Introduction — the current contributions are too dense and unfocused. Each one runs 3-8 lines and packs in too many details: the first contribution alone lists the 83.3% finding, baseline robustness, 99% threshold, shuffle control, 27 strategies, and 9 models all at once. For a strong paper, each contribution should be punchy and self-contained, maybe 2-3 lines maximum. Let me reframe them more crisply: the first should focus on the core finding about symbolic verification becoming vacuous under self-extraction, the second on the diagnostic framework itself, and the third on what ProcessSim reveals about independence.

Actually, looking at my revised version, I've tightened them considerably — each is now 3-4 lines instead of 5-8 — but the Director also wants me to de-emphasize the third contribution about process-level independence. That means I should either fold it into the second contribution or drop it entirely and make the paper's story rest on the first two: the Symbolic Mirage problem and the diagnostic framework that solves it.

So I'm merging those three contributions down to two core ones, which brings the total from about 16 lines down to 7. Much cleaner. Now I need to plan the execution: write the updated plan, get Director approval, then execute section by section starting with the foundational Method & Setup, moving into Results, then the analysis sections.

For the file restructuring, I'm consolidating the existing tex files — method.tex stays as the foundation, experiments.tex becomes the Results section, analysis.tex gets merged into the new Symbolic Mirage section, and solutions.tex becomes the Escaping the Bottleneck section. I'll need to rewrite method.tex to incorporate setup details, trim experiments.tex to focus on the data and regime analysis, and consolidate the diagnostic content into a restructured analysis file.

Now I'm drafting the writing_plan.yaml as a comprehensive guide that references the paper-writing-norms skill for the workers to consult. I also need to address the Director's note about the Symbolic Mirage Hypothesis — Predictions 1 and 2 are post-hoc observations, while only Prediction 3 is a genuine forward-looking prediction, so I should clarify this distinction in the method section where the hypothesis is introduced. I'm deciding to remove those empirical finding boxes entirely and integrate them as regular paragraphs in section 5 instead—they'll feel less like proven theorems that way. Given the deadline of 5/25 and that it's already 5/23, I need to work through a tight two-day schedule: tackle the method, results, and symbolic mirage sections today, then finish the remaining sections, figures, and consistency checks tomorrow before final submission.

Now I'm mapping out the actual section structure. The current paper has introduction, related work, background and setup, experiments with the main results table, analysis covering effective-K and SCB, and cross-architecture sections. I'm consolidating this into a cleaner flow: introduction, related work, merged method and setup, results with the regime analysis, the symbolic mirage analysis, escaping the bottleneck for cross-architecture findings, and discussion.

The key moves are pulling experimental setup into the methods section, promoting regime analysis into results, consolidating the symbolic mirage concept into its own section with diagnostics and the hypothesis, moving the process-kappa figure to appendix, and significantly expanding the discussion. This is a substantial reorganization that should improve the narrative flow.

Now I'm thinking through what the abstract needs to do differently. The current version leads with the saturation problem, but the new framing should open with the fundamental tension: can formal verification actually help LLM reasoning when the model extracts its own constraints? I want to add a caveat about power limitations and dial back the cross-architecture generalization, while keeping the diagnostic findings intact.

The key results I need to capture are stark: the formal layer adds nothing on most problems, self-extracted constraints are systematically biased toward wrong answers even when they pass validation, and attempts to fix this fail across the board. But the oracle experiments show the approach itself is sound—the bottleneck is the extraction, not the verification.

For the next part, I'm noting that self-extraction only captures about 12% of the theoretical ceiling, though I should include the caveat that ten of the sixteen conditions tested are underpowered. The zero-cost diagnostics are promising for predicting when aggregation will work, and there's some initial evidence from cross-architecture NLI verification that we might escape this constraint, though I should be more cautious about that claim.

I'm also reconsidering the title—the current one focuses on self-consistency, but "The Symbolic Mirage" better captures the core finding that formal verification creates an illusion of correctness without actually improving reasoning. I think that's the stronger framing, so I'll go with that and prepare the YAML for submission.

Before I finalize the plan, I'm catching some data inconsistencies: the solutions.tex file still has outdated numbers (39.33/+6.67) that should reflect the corrected values (39.17/+7.00) from the latest update, and introduction.tex has the same stale "+6.67pp" figure on line 28. I'll need to flag these discrepancies in my plan so they get corrected during the restructuring.

# Writing Plan — symb_invariant_consensus
# V4 STRATEGIC RESTRUCTURE: Presentation-first upgrade for 4.0+
# Target: EMNLP 2026 ARR May cycle, DDL 2026-05-25
# Updated: 2026-05-23T16:00:00Z

meta:
  venue: EMNLP 2026
  track: main (ARR May cycle)
  template: docs/paper/acl.sty
  page_limit: 8
  deadline: 2026-05-25
  title: >
    Beyond Self-Consistency: Why Self-Extracted Constraints
    Fail to Improve LLM Logical Reasoning
  title_alternative: >
    The Symbolic Mirage: Why Formal Self-Verification
    Adds No Information Beyond Majority Voting
  title_note: >
    Alternative title is punchier and highlights the paradox.
    Director decides. Current title is safe; alternative is higher-impact.
  core_claim: >
    Provably sound Z3 verification becomes informationally vacuous
    under self-extraction: MAX-SAT agrees with majority voting on
    94.4% of problems because self-extracted constraints inherit
    the model's distributional bias (BR 1.66-4.97x across nine models).
    Three zero-cost diagnostics classify all 60 tested conditions.
    Cross-architecture NLI provides preliminary evidence of escaping
    the bottleneck.
  paper_type: >
    Diagnostic negative-result paper with constructive escape.
    Primary value: quantified diagnosis + practitioner framework.
  previous_version: "v3 (2026-05-20): G+R Dual Method (abandoned)"
  change_rationale: >
    Round 14 scored 3.5. Soundness is strong (4/5) but Significance
    (2.5-3.5) and Presentation drag. Reviewer pathway to 4.0+ is
    presentation improvement, not new experiments. V4 restructures
    for: (1) narrative clarity, (2) display-item redistribution,
    (3) abbreviation reduction, (4) depth rebalancing.

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# DIAGNOSIS: 7 Problems → 7 Solutions
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
restructure_rationale:

  problem_1_info_density:
    issue: "13 technical abbreviations in 8 pages"
    solution: "Reduce to 6 essential abbreviations"
    keep: [SC, SICA, BR, "K_eff", NLI, MAX-SAT]
    eliminate:
      - SCB: "spell out 'symbolic confirmation bias' (use abbreviation only in tables)"
      - CJT: "spell out 'Condorcet Jury Theorem' (only used 2-3 times)"
      - CCR: "appendix only"
      - DRC: "appendix only"
      - ICG: "spell out 'iterative constraint generation'"
      - ProcessSim: "use 'process similarity'"
      - TOST: "spell out or remove from main text"
      - FOL: "use 'logical constraints' or spell out"
    net_reduction: "13 → 6 abbreviations (-54%)"

  problem_2_depth_imbalance:
    issue: "§3.1 CJT (half page, non-original) vs §5.4 Remediation (15 lines, major finding) vs §7 Discussion (1/3 page)"
    solution: |
      - CJT: 2 sentences in intro (save 0.4 pages)

[Director 指令] **补充指令：理论深度强化 — A/B/C/D 四个方向全做**

用户要求在写作重构的同时，加强论文的理论深度和概念强度。**质量优先于速度**。以下四个方向全部纳入你的 writing_plan：

## A. SCB 概率证明（最高优先级）

把 Symbolic Confirmation Bias 从"经验观察"升级为"理论结果"。构建简单概率模型：

- 模型 M 对问题 q 生成答案 a_M
- 从包含 a_M 的 trace 提取约束 c
- 证明 E[BR] ≥ 1：P(c supports a_M | a_M ≠ a*) > P(c supports a* | a_M ≠ a*)

核心洞察：约束 c 是 trace 的有损函数，trace 已经包含 a_M → c 继承 a_M 的分布先验。这是信息论上的必然，不是模型能力问题。

目标：在 §3.3 或 §5.2 中用 1-2 段给出 clean 的形式化论证。不需要长证明，要 elegant。

## B. CIL（Cumulative Information Lift）信息论指标

形式化定义：CIL(V, G) = I(V_output; ground_truth | G_answer)

- Self-extraction → CIL ≈ 0（约束不含超出答案的信息）
- Cross-architecture → CIL > 0（独立模型带来新信息）

这个指标如果能统一解释所有条件的 combo gain 方向，就比 K_eff + BR + C₀ 三个 ad hoc 指标更优雅。**这可能需要 Agent 用已有实验数据计算 mutual information**——如果你确定需要哪些数据，列出来，我让 Agent 准备。

## C. Capability Gap 理论模型

当前 capability gap 只有 n=6 的经验观察。需要一个简单的理论推导：

假设 verifier V（准确率 V_acc）与 generator G（准确率 SC_G）条件独立，推导 combo gain 与 SC_G 的关系。至少要能解释为什么 gain 随 SC_G 单调递减——当 SC_G → 1 时 gain → 0（天花板），当 SC_G 很低时 gain 受 V_acc 上界控制。

## D. 因果 DAG

画一张 M → T → A → C → S 的因果图，用 d-separation 论证 C ⊥ ground_truth | A。这张图直观解释了 self-extraction 失败的信息论根源：**约束的所有信息都经过"答案"这个瓶颈节点**。

可放在 §3.3（方法论基础）或作为 Figure 插入 pages 3-5 的文字墙区域（一举两得：加理论深度 + 打破纯文字）。

## 与写作重构的关系

这四个方向应该融入你的整体重构方案：
- A + D 可能改变 §3.3 Symbolic Mirage 的整个写法（从 ad hoc hypothesis → 有理论支撑的 framework）
- B 可能影响 §5 或 §6 的结构（CIL 作为统一指标替代部分 diagnostics）
- C 强化 §6 的理论基础

**质量要求**：
- 形式化论证要 rigorous 但 accessible——审稿人是 NLP 背景，不是数学家
- 每个理论结果要与已有经验数据对应（理论预测 X，实验验证 X）
- 不要为了加理论而牺牲可读性——如果推导太长，核心结果放正文，完整证明放附录

请把这四个方向整合进 writing_plan.yaml 一起提交审批。如果需要 Agent 计算新数据（比如 CIL），在 plan 中标注清楚。

# Writing Plan — symb_invariant_consensus
# V4 STRATEGIC RESTRUCTURE: Presentation-first upgrade for 4.0+
# Target: EMNLP 2026 ARR May cycle, DDL 2026-05-25
# Updated: 2026-05-23T16:00:00Z

meta:
  venue: EMNLP 2026
  track: main (ARR May cycle)
  template: docs/paper/acl.sty
  page_limit: 8
  deadline: 2026-05-25
  title: >
    Beyond Self-Consistency: Why Self-Extracted Constraints
    Fail to Improve LLM Logical Reasoning
  title_alternative: >
    The Symbolic Mirage: Why Formal Self-Verification
    Adds No Information Beyond Majority Voting
  title_note: >
    Alternative title is punchier and highlights the paradox.
    Director decides. Current title is safe; alternative is higher-impact.
  core_claim: >
    Provably sound Z3 verification becomes informationally vacuous
    under self-extraction: MAX-SAT agrees with majority voting on
    94.4% of problems because self-extracted constraints inherit
    the model's distributional bias (BR 1.66-4.97x across nine models).
    Three zero-cost diagnostics classify all 60 tested conditions.
    Cross-architecture NLI provides preliminary evidence of escaping
    the bottleneck.
  paper_type: >
    Diagnostic negative-result paper with constructive escape.
    Primary value: quantified diagnosis + practitioner framework.

    net_reduction: "13 → 6 abbreviations (-54%)"

  problem_2_depth_imbalance:
    issue: "§3.1 CJT (half page, non-original) vs §5.4 Remediation (15 lines, major finding) vs §7 Discussion (1/3 page)"

  problem_3_text_wall:
    issue: "Pages 3-5 have zero display items (Related Work + Background & Setup)"
    solution: |
      - Move experimental setup into §3 Method → Table 1 appears ~page 4-5 (was page 6)
      - Move regime scatter figure into §4 Results → visual relief on page 5
      - Add diagnostic decision tree figure in §5 → another display item
      - Net: every 2-page spread gets at least one display item

  problem_4_mirage_hypothesis:
    issue: "Empirical Finding 1-2 are post-hoc observations in theorem-like boxes; only P1 is testable"
    solution: |
      - Remove Finding 1 and Finding 2 tcolorboxes from §3
      - Remove O1/O2/P1 labels (too formulaic for observations)
      - Present the Mirage Hypothesis in §5 AFTER showing SCB data
      - Frame as: "Three patterns emerge from the data → we formulate the Symbolic Mirage"
      - The hypothesis is then TESTED by §6 (cross-architecture)

  problem_5_cross_arch_overstatement:
    issue: "Cross-architecture results treated as established finding; only Mistral-7B is significant"
    solution: |
      - "escapes the bottleneck" → "preliminary evidence of escaping"
      - "validates" → "is consistent with"
      - Add explicit caveat: "significant only for Mistral-7B (SC below verifier)"
      - In abstract: add "on the weakest generator" qualifier
      - Section title: "Escaping the Bottleneck" → keep (describes aspiration)

  problem_6_power_caveat:
    issue: "10/16 conditions underpowered; abstract doesn't acknowledge"

      - Abstract: add "with equivalence established in four conditions,
        ten remaining underpowered for effects below ~2 percentage points"

  problem_7_surprise:
    issue: "Core finding predictable after Huang et al.; Z3 specificity underemphasized"
    solution: |
      Reframe the hook throughout the paper:
      - OLD: "Another self-correction failure study"
      - NEW: "Even provably sound formal verification becomes vacuous under self-extraction"
      Key differentiators to emphasize:
      1. Z3 is a FORMAL solver (not another LLM trick) — provably correct
      2. 99% of constraints pass Z3 validation — no syntax issues
      3. Oracle controls prove the MECHANISM works (+30pp possible)
      4. The failure is specifically in EXTRACTION — new kind of bias
      5. MAX-SAT = majority voting on 94.4% of problems — the formal apparatus is a "mirage"
      This is distinct from Huang: they show NL self-correction fails;
      we show FORMAL self-verification fails even with a correct solver.

input.new_string:
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# THEORETICAL DEPTH ENHANCEMENTS (A/B/C/D)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
theoretical_enhancements:

  A_scb_proof:
    priority: highest
    placement: "§3.2 (The Information Bottleneck)"
    space_cost: "~5 lines + 1 equation = ~0.10 pages"
    core_argument: |
      Proposition (BR ≥ 1 under same-trace coupling):
      When a_M ≠ a* (model errs), n_M > n_* by definition of majority.
      Under same-trace coupling (constraint c supports its source trace's
      answer), |C_{a_M}| ∝ n_M and |C_{a*}| ∝ n_*.
      Therefore BR = n_M / n_* > 1.
      This is a mathematical necessity, not an empirical finding.
    key_equation: >
      BR = |C_{a_M}| / |C_{a*}| = n_M / n_* > 1
      (when a_M ≠ a*, by definition of majority voting)
    validation: >
      Shuffle control: BR_null ≈ BR_obs (p > 0.7) confirms the bias
      is structural — proportional to trace-count distribution, not
      extraction-specific error.
    elegance_note: >
      The proof is 3 lines. Core insight: constraints are a lossy function
      of traces that already contain the answer. BR > 1 follows from the
      definition of majority voting. No assumptions about model capability.

  B_cil:
    priority: high
    placement: "§3.2 (definition) + §5/§6 (empirical)"
    space_cost: "~4 lines + 1 equation = ~0.08 pages"
    definition: |
      CIL(V, G) = I(V_output; GT | G_answer)
      "How much does the verifier add beyond the generator's answer?"
    theoretical_predictions:
      self_extraction: >
        CIL ≈ 0. By the causal DAG (D), C ⊥ GT | A, so self-extracted
        constraints contain no information about ground truth beyond
        the generator's answer. This is the information-theoretic
        restatement of SCB.
      cross_architecture: >
        CIL > 0 when V has an independent information path to GT
        (i.e., V does not share M's distributional prior).
    operationalization: >
      CIL is the theoretical ideal. We operationalize it through the
      Conditional Correction Ratio (CCR; Appendix D):
      CCR(V,G) = log[P(V correct | G wrong) / P(V correct | G correct)]
      CCR > 0 ↔ CIL > 0 (verifier preferentially corrects errors).
      Empirical CCR correlates with combo gain: ρ = 0.84, p = 0.014.
    data_needs: >
      No new computation needed. Existing CCR data (8 conditions in
      Appendix D) serves as the empirical proxy. The d-separation
      argument gives CIL ≈ 0 for self-extraction theoretically.
      OPTIONAL: Agent could compute actual MI values from per-problem
      (G_answer, V_output, GT) tuples in combo data for a cleaner
      presentation. Flag as nice-to-have, not blocking.

  C_capability_gap:
    priority: medium
    placement: "§6.1 (before empirical results)"
    space_cost: "~5 lines + 1 equation = ~0.10 pages"
    derivation: |
      Under conditional independence between G (accuracy SC_G) and V
      (accuracy V_acc):
      ΔCombo ≈ (1 - SC_G) · V_acc - SC_G · (1 - V_acc)
             = V_acc - SC_G
      Properties:
      - Monotonically decreasing in SC_G ✓
      - ΔCombo = 0 when SC_G = V_acc (breakeven at capability parity) ✓
      - ΔCombo > 0 when SC_G < V_acc (verifier stronger) ✓
      - As SC_G → 1, gain → 0 (ceiling: few errors to correct) ✓
    empirical_validation: >
      DeBERTa standalone V_acc = 55%. Model predicts breakeven at
      SC_G ≈ 55%. Empirically: Mistral (SC 39%) gains (+7pp),
      all generators above 72% show no significant gain.
      Spearman ρ = 1.0, p = 0.003, n=6 matches the monotonic prediction.
      Magnitude attenuated vs linear model due to imperfect independence
      and vote-weighting mechanics — state this as expected.
    note: >
      This is a first-order approximation. State it as such:
      "Under a simplified independence model..." with the caveat that
      real combo voting involves weighted margins.

  D_causal_dag:
    priority: highest
    placement: "§3.2 (The Information Bottleneck) — as Figure"
    space_cost: "~0.20 pages (TikZ figure, single-column)"
    dag_structure: |
      Self-extraction DAG:
        Q → GT (ground truth)
        Q, M → T (trace)
        T → A (answer, contained in trace)
        T, M → C (constraint, extracted by same model)
        {A, C} → S (MAX-SAT score)

      d-separation: C ⊥ GT | A
      All paths from C to GT: C ← (T,M) ← Q → GT
      Conditioning on A (which is T → A) blocks the chain.
      Interpretation: constraints carry no information about GT
      beyond what's already in the answer.
    cross_arch_contrast: |
      Cross-architecture DAG:
        Q → GT
        Q, M_G → T → A → S
        Q, M_V → V_out → S (independent path)

      V_out ⊥̸ GT | A because V has an independent path Q → M_V → V_out
      that doesn't pass through A. Hence CIL > 0.
    figure_design: >
      Two-panel TikZ figure (a) Self-extraction (b) Cross-architecture.
      Panel (a): show A as an information bottleneck node (highlighted).
      Panel (b): show V_out with independent path to GT (highlighted).
      Compact, ~0.5 column width per panel. Breaks pages 3-4 text wall.
      Gray/blue color scheme matching Figure 1.

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# NEW SECTION STRUCTURE
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
